old_problem: The historical review left single-record OOB deletion Pending because the Master supplies no target and a real SDR may have monitoring dependencies. IPMI 2.0 defines the 22h reservation, volatile Record ID behavior, same-reservation 23h revalidation, exact 26h request/returned-ID and Delete capability. A dedicated inert disposable fixture absent from a captured pre-fixture baseline safely parameterizes target and recovery; the test need not guess a production record or use Clear SDR.
disposition_reason: Use only one pre-provisioned owner-approved disposable SDR absent from the pre-fixture canonical repository and without live sensor/control dependency. Bind the OOB endpoint, export the entire current repository and fixture, obtain one fresh 22h reservation, and under that same reservation reconstruct the target with 23h to revalidate current non-selector RID, stable key and body immediately before confirmation. Send 26h once with reservation LS/MS plus RID LS/MS; require completion 00h and identical returned RID. Enumerate by stable key—not the recyclable old RID—to prove exactly the fixture disappeared and canonical repository/monitoring state equals pre-fixture baseline. Unsupported is capability-backed N/A. Never delete production/unknown data, use 0000h/FFFFh, reuse a stale RID, clear the repository, cross-credit IB or retry.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1211-1214, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests.json, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. The corresponding IB Delete row 1086/new review event 227 and OOB Add/Partial Add setup paths were read while retaining distinct coverage. Formal queue sequence 87 was read from the locked queue and verified as row 1214 / variant 8e602d1b14e0686e.

IPMI v2.0 Appendix G assigns Delete SDR to Storage NetFn 0Ah/Cmd 26h. Section 33.15 defines exactly four request bytes—Reservation ID LS/MS followed by Record ID LS/MS—and returns the deleted Record ID LS/MS after completion.

Delete is optional and Get SDR Repository Info operation-support bit 3 reports it. N/A requires authoritative read-only/Delete-unsupported evidence; an OOB authentication, privilege, network or timeout error is not capability evidence.

Section 33.11 requires a current reservation. A qualifying repository change cancels it, making reservation a race detector rather than a permanent lock. The final 23h identity read and 26h must use the same reservation with no intervening Reserve or writer.

Section 33.8 makes Record IDs volatile/recyclable handles. Target selection uses stable record type/key/body and complete current bytes, not an ordinal or historical RID; 0000h and FFFFh selector values are prohibited.

After deletion the old RID may be assigned to another record. A failed read of that RID is not the acceptance oracle; bounded sequential enumeration must show the stable key absent and every unrelated canonical record present.

A separately provisioned disposable fixture gives real Delete coverage while restoring an independently captured PRE_FIXTURE_BASELINE. It has one unique key, bounded/no monitoring effect and no retention/incident dependency, so no production definition is selected.

Add/delete can reassign other RIDs and update timestamps. Reconciliation therefore compares the canonical multiset of version/type/stable-key/body plus count/capacity/overflow and monitoring state, while retaining raw ID/timestamp changes as evidence.

Exact fixture bytes are also the owner reconstruction artifact for an unexpected loss, but re-add is an emergency action under the separately reviewed Add/Partial Add identity, never an automatic step that could mask a failed deletion.

OOB endpoint-to-asset binding, secret-safe authentication and session evidence are mandatory. The corresponding IB Delete cannot satisfy this Source Key, and an OOB transport failure cannot be reclassified as unsupported.

ED-02 preserves Source Key/variant; ED-03 protects OEM meaning; ED-13/ED-15 govern N/A and criteria; ED-17 preserves exports/logs; ED-19 separates IB/OOB; ED-28/ED-30 require recovery/approval; ED-34 parameterizes the fixture; ED-38 prohibits retry.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Delete SDR (OOB Storage 0Ah/26h) same-reservation identity proof and disposable-record removal
test_case.purpose: Delete exactly one disposable SDR through the authenticated OOB path after proving the current RID still belongs to its approved stable key/body, verify no unrelated repository or monitoring coverage is lost, and return to the pre-fixture logical baseline without Clear SDR or IB substitution.
required_package: Approved BMC/SUT/firmware and host-verified secret-safe LANPlus endpoint bound to FRU/serial, with authoritative Repository Info Delete-support bit and working 22h, 23h and 26h

Dedicated inert DELETE_FIXTURE created through a separately reviewed setup: unique standard/OEM type/key/body, current RID, exact raw bytes, IANA/owner authority, dependency proof and expected no/bounded monitoring effect
Immutable PRE_FIXTURE_BASELINE and current PREDELETE repository export, canonicalized by version/type/stable-key/body while retaining raw records, RIDs and timestamps

Pinned credential-safe no-retry OOB runner, fresh-reservation bounded 23h reader, exact 26h builder, sequential post-delete enumerator and comparator for count/free space/erase timestamp/overflow and monitoring state
Immediate record-specific confirmation, maintenance/incident/retention clearance and owner-held exact reconstruction artifact usable only through separately reviewed Add/Partial Add recovery
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED SINGLE-RECORD OOB DELETE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Bind BMC DNS/IP, FRU/serial and firmware to the intended SUT and protect credentials outside command arguments/logs. Record 20h Delete support; load immutable PRE_FIXTURE_BASELINE and export the entire PREDELETE repository. Require exactly one DELETE_FIXTURE stable key, prove it absent from PRE_FIXTURE_BASELINE, inert or bounded by the approved effect oracle, free of retention/incident hold and currently mapped to a RID other than 0000h/FFFFh. Compare all other canonical records to PRE_FIXTURE_BASELINE. Obtain one fresh 0Ah/22h reservation R over the verified session. Without reserving again, reconstruct target with bounded 0Ah/23h reads using R and require exact fixture type/key/body/RID; stop on cancellation, session change or mismatch. Display endpoint, R, RID, stable key, record hash, expected post-state and reconstruction artifact for immediate confirmation. Send exactly once: `ipmitool ... raw 0x0a 0x26 Rlo Rhi RIDlo RIDhi`. Require completion 00h and returned RID equal request. Do not retry. Sequentially enumerate from first to last and search by stable key; do not assume old RID becomes invalid. Require zero fixture matches, count one lower than PREDELETE/equal PRE_FIXTURE_BASELINE, coherent free-space/erase metadata, overflow unchanged, exact canonical PRE_FIXTURE_BASELINE equality and approved monitoring/alert/control state. Keep row-1214 Clear and row-1086 IB separate.
test_case.expected_result: The same-reservation OOB precheck proves the selected current RID maps to the one approved disposable key/body. One exact 26h request completes 00h and returns that RID. Post-delete sequential enumeration contains no matching stable key, retains every unrelated canonical record, restores count/logical content to PRE_FIXTURE_BASELINE, changes capacity/erase metadata coherently and causes only the approved monitoring effect; volatile RIDs/timestamps may differ. Unsupported Delete is evidence-backed N/A. Identity race, wrong/multiple missing record, dependency loss, transport ambiguity or recovery divergence is FAIL/NOT READY without another delete.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact OOB Source Key/variant and endpoint binding, authoritative Delete support, one disposable fixture and two-level baseline, fresh reservation, complete same-reservation 23h target proof, immediate confirmation, one exact 26h request, matching returned RID, stable-key absence, all unrelated canonical records intact and pre-fixture monitoring recovery. FAIL covers stale/unverified RID, selector IDs, live/held/unknown record, completion without returned-ID/full enumeration, relying on old-RID failure, unrelated loss/effect, credential exposure, Clear/IB substitution, raw-hash-only comparison, retry or unresolved recovery. NOT READY covers absent fixture/baseline/dependency proof/Delete capability/reader/approval/reconstruction artifact. N/A requires authoritative Delete-unsupported evidence, not transport failure.
safety_gate: Target only a dedicated disposable fixture with a unique stable key and no irreplaceable monitoring role. Never select a production sensor, threshold, locator, association or unknown OEM record.
Bind endpoint to FRU/serial/firmware and keep secrets out of process arguments/logs. Target/session uncertainty stops before reservation or delete.
Preserve complete raw PRE_FIXTURE and PREDELETE exports plus canonical comparisons. Do not clear SDR, SEL or OS logs and do not execute the source boilerplate's clear step.
Use one fresh reservation unchanged from final 23h identity proof through 26h. Cancellation, RID/key/body drift or any concurrent writer stops without retry.
Display exact endpoint, RID and stable record hash for immediate approval. Never send 0000h, FFFFh, wildcard, adjacent or prior-run RID.
Verify by sequential stable-key enumeration/canonical content, not old-RID failure. Other RIDs may legitimately move.
No automatic retry or second delete. On ambiguous completion enumerate once and stop; unexpected loss freezes all repository writes for owner reconstruction—never clear/reset or improvise re-add.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant; BMC/SUT/firmware/FRU and OOB endpoint/channel binding; official reservation/RID/26h authority and Delete capability; distinct Clear and IB identities
Immutable PRE_FIXTURE/PREDELETE raw exports, canonical key/body multisets, repository info and monitoring/dependency/retention audit
Fixture source/hash/type/key/body/current RID, OEM authority if applicable, uniqueness proof and exact owner reconstruction artifact
Fresh reservation and session, complete same-reservation 23h target reconstruction, displayed action and immediate confirmation
Exact redacted 26h request/completion/returned RID and full sequential stable-key search with count/capacity/erase/overflow comparison
All unrelated canonical records and sensor/inventory/alert/control state preserved, final PASS/FAIL/NOT READY/N/A and explicit statement that the review agent executed no DUT action
test_case.recovery: Successful deletion of the fixture is the planned return to PRE_FIXTURE_BASELINE. If 26h completion is ambiguous, do not resend: enumerate once by stable key and compare canonical content. If fixture remains, preserve it as inert failed-test state and hand cleanup to the owner; if absent and all else matches, record the transport ambiguity without rerunning. If any unrelated record changed or disappeared, stop every write, preserve raw exports/session/monitoring evidence and let the owner reconstruct only the exact affected record under separately authorized Add/Partial Add. Never Clear SDR, reset, switch to IB or automatically retry.

source_conflict.reason: IPMI 2.0 resolves reservation, 26h request/response, capability and volatile-RID semantics. The Review layer safely parameterizes one disposable target and replaces TBD/log clearing with stable-key verification and canonical reconciliation.

blocked.reason: A standard exact-one-record delete and race-safe identity method exist. Endpoint, disposable fixture, dependency audit and reconstruction artifact are bounded Project prerequisites rather than missing core semantics.

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7
external_authorities.application: Sections 33.8 and 33.11-33.16 plus Appendix G define volatile/recyclable SDR Record IDs, reservation ownership/cancellation, Get SDR identity verification, optional Delete support and exact Storage 0Ah/Cmd26h request/returned RID.

project_authority: The SDR/BMC owner provisions and identifies the disposable fixture, proves dependencies/retention, supplies pre-fixture/pre-delete baselines, confirms Delete support, authorizes endpoint/RID and holds reconstruction material. It cannot authorize wildcard/stale IDs, unknown live records, Clear/IB substitution, completion-only PASS, retry, credential exposure or recovery that hides collateral deletion.
